text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Sultan of Selangor state said he had not vetoed Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's decision of suitable candidates for the post of chief minister of the state.
-- The state government of Johor is to submit a proposal to the Works Ministry on Wednesday to impose a levy on all Singapore-registered cars entering Malaysia via the causeway.

-- The number of companies compulsorily wound up by courts increased to 26 in 1996, compared to 24 in 1995, said the Registrar of Companies in its latest annual report. The total number of companies liquidated in 1996 stood at 681.
